Conta la LIC stimata dall'R2*: 4,3 mg/g: What counts is the LIC estimated from R2*: 4.3 mg/g is above normal (up to about 1.8-2 mg/g), and the collection classes it as «Mild». Some tables place the liver T2* limit around 6 ms, but with biopsy calibrations (such as Garbowski's) a normal LIC corresponds to a T2* of about 15 ms or more.

Il ferro accorcia il T2*: nelle sequenze: Iron shortens T2*: in multi-echo gradient-echo sequences the signal of iron-loaded tissue falls faster the more iron there is. You draw an ROI and fit a curve S(TE) = S0·e^(−TE/T2*); R2* = 1000/T2* (s⁻¹). Heart: full-thickness ROI on the interventricular septum of the mid-ventricular short-axis slice (away from the susceptibility artifacts of the cardiac veins and lung in the lateral wall). Cardiac thresholds at 1.5 T: T2* > 20 ms normal, 10-20 ms mild-moderate overload, < 10 ms severe. Liver: ROI in the right-lobe parenchyma away from vessels; the liver iron concentration (LIC, mg Fe/g dry weight) is estimated from R2* with a calibration curve (the collection uses Garbowski 2014: LIC ≈ 0.029·R2*^1.014). Most used LIC classes: < 2 mg/g normal (up to about 1.8), 2-7 mild, 7-15 moderate, > 15 severe. With very low signal, noise creates a «floor»: a fit on all echoes overestimates T2*; truncation of the late echoes or a model with a constant (offset) is used. In the viewer, the T2* tool (More measurements → T2*) copies the ROI to all echoes of the slice, shows the curve, T2* and R2* with both models and, for the liver, the LIC. In this girl the septum stays grey up to the last echoes (T2* 33.9 ms in the collection: normal), while the liver darkens gradually: T2* 7.4 ms, R2* 138 s⁻¹, LIC 4.3 mg/g, mild overload. Be careful not to read the liver T2* with the cardiac thresholds: for the liver, reason on the LIC. It is a picture of good chelation control: report with the values and continue periodic follow-up.
